title: How to Lower Your Risk of Dementia Starting in Middle Age
titleZh: 如何从中年开始降低患痴呆症的风险
credits: Lauran Neergaard reported this story for the Associated Press. Jill Robbins adapted it for Learning English.

sentences.en: New research suggests the risk of Americans developing dementia over a lifetime may be much higher than once thought.
sentences.zh: 新的研究表明，美国人一生中患阿尔茨海默病的风险可能比以往认为的要高得多。

sentences.en: A new study predicts about one million Americans will likely develop the disease each year by 2060.
sentences.zh: 一项新研究预测，到2060年，美国每年可能有约100万人可能患上这种疾病。

sentences.en: That is about twice the number of people estimated in earlier studies.
sentences.zh: 这大约是早期研究中估计人数的两倍。

sentences.en: The new finding is based on a large study involving a team from major U.S. medical centers and other research organizations.
sentences.zh: 这一新发现基于一项大型研究，涉及美国主要医学中心的一个团队以及其他研究机构。

sentences.en: It recently appeared in the publication Nature Medicine.
sentences.zh: 该研究最近发表在《自然医学》期刊上。

sentences.en: The study found that after age 55, people face up to a 42 percent chance of developing dementia, if they live long enough.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，55岁之后，如果寿命足够长，人们患阿尔茨海默病的概率高达42%。

sentences.en: The research showed the risk of dementia is highest after age 75.
sentences.zh: 这项研究表明，75岁之后患阿尔茨海默病的风险最高。

sentences.en: But the good news is that there are steps people can take to reduce the risks.
sentences.zh: 但好消息是，人们可以采取一些措施来降低风险。

sentences.en: One of them is controlling high blood pressure and other conditions, such as diabetes or being severely overweight, meaning obese.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是控制高血压以及糖尿病或严重超重（即肥胖）等其他疾病。

sentences.en: Health experts advise everyone, even those in middle age, to take steps to avoid such problems.
sentences.zh: 健康专家建议所有人，包括中年人在内，都采取措施避免这些问题。

sentences.en: Dr. Josef Coresh of NYU Langone Health was a lead writer of the study.
sentences.zh: 纽约大学朗格尼健康的约瑟夫·科雷斯博士是该研究的主要作者之一。

sentences.en: He told The Associated Press, "All of our research suggests what you do in midlife really matters.”
sentences.zh: 他告诉美联社，"我们所有的研究都表明，你在中年时期所做的事确实很重要。"

sentences.en: It can be quite common for older people to take longer to remember a name or where they placed certain objects.
sentences.zh: 老年人需要更长时间才能想起某个名字或某件物品放在哪里，这种情况其实相当常见。

sentences.en: But research on dementia suggests it is not a normal part of aging.
sentences.zh: 但对阿尔茨海默病的研究表明，它并不是衰老的正常组成部分。

sentences.en: Rather, the disease is a progressive loss of memory, language and other cognitive abilities over time.
sentences.zh: 相反，这种疾病是随时间推移记忆、语言及其他认知能力的进行性丧失。

sentences.en: Getting older is currently the biggest risk and the U.S. population is aging at a fast rate.
sentences.zh: 目前，衰老是最大的风险因素，而美国人口正以很快的速度老龄化。

sentences.en: Dementia has many forms, the most common being Alzheimer's.
sentences.zh: 阿尔茨海默病有多种类型，最常见的是阿尔茨海默病。

sentences.en: Because the disease is linked to silent changes in the brain, signs or symptoms of dementia might not start showing until many years later.
sentences.zh: 由于这种疾病与大脑中不易察觉的变化有关，阿尔茨海默病的迹象或症状可能要多年之后才会显现。

sentences.en: Other kinds include vascular dementia, when heart disease or small strokes limit blood flow to the brain.
sentences.zh: 其他类型包括血管性痴呆，即心脏病或小中风限制了流向大脑的血液。

sentences.en: Many people also have mixed causes, meaning vascular problems could worsen existing dementia.
sentences.zh: 许多人同时有多种病因，意味着血管问题可能加重已有的阿尔茨海默病。

sentences.en: Dr. James Galvin is an Alzheimer's specialist at the University of Miami.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·加尔文博士是迈阿密大学阿尔茨海默病的专家。

sentences.en: He noted that aging by itself is "not a guarantee that someone will develop dementia."
sentences.zh: 他指出，衰老本身"并不能保证某人一定会患痴呆症。"

sentences.en: Galvin was not involved in the new study.
sentences.zh: 加尔文并未参与这项新研究。

sentences.en: But he said the latest findings on that support previous research.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，最新研究结果支持了此前的研究。

sentences.en: Earlier studies estimated about 14 percent of men and 23 percent of women would develop some form of dementia during their lifetime.
sentences.zh: 此前的研究估计，约14%的男性和23%的女性在一生中会患上某种形式的痴呆症。

sentences.en: Since women live longer than men, they are more likely to get it.
sentences.zh: 由于女性比男性活得更久，她们更有可能患上此病。

sentences.en: But the latest research examined more recent data from a U.S. study that followed the heart health and cognitive abilities of about 15,000 older adults from 1987 until 2020.
sentences.zh: 但最新研究分析了美国一项研究的较新数据，该研究从1987年追踪约1.5万名老年人的心脏健康与认知能力，直至2020年。

sentences.en: In that group, the risk for dementia averaged 35 percent for men and 48 percent for women.
sentences.zh: 在这一群体中，患痴呆症的风险平均为男性35%、女性48%。

sentences.en: One reason for the different rates is that the group of people studied lived longer.
sentences.zh: 造成这一差异的原因之一是，所研究的人群活得更久。

sentences.en: The study shows how the risk changes with additional years of life.
sentences.zh: 这项研究展示了风险如何随寿命延长而变化。

sentences.en: Only 4 percent of people developed dementia between the ages of 55 and 75.
sentences.zh: 在55岁至75岁之间，仅有4%的人患上了痴呆症。

sentences.en: Coresh describes this difference as an important 20-year window for protecting brain health.
sentences.zh: 科雷什将这一差异描述为保护大脑健康的一个重要的20年窗口期。

sentences.en: For people surviving common health threats until 75, the dementia risk then jumped — to 20 percent by age 85 and 42 percent between the ages of 85 and 95.
sentences.zh: 对于能够抵御常见健康威胁而活到75岁的人来说，此后患痴呆症的风险陡然上升——到85岁时升至20%，在85岁至95岁之间则为42%。

sentences.en: Black Americans had a slightly higher risk, 44 percent, than white individuals at 41 percent.
sentences.zh: 黑人的患病风险略高，为44%，而白人为41%。

sentences.en: There are some health risks people cannot control.
sentences.zh: 有些健康风险是个人无法控制的。

sentences.en: Besides age, people can inherit a gene version, or variant, called APOE4.
sentences.zh: 除了年龄之外，人们还可能遗传一种名为APOE4的基因版本，即变异体。

sentences.en: This can raise the risk of getting Alzheimer's later in life.
sentences.zh: 这会提高晚年罹患阿尔茨海默病的风险。

sentences.en: But medical researchers have identified some things people can do to delay, or possibly even prevent developing dementia.
sentences.zh: 但医学研究者已经找出了一些人们可以采取措施，以延缓、甚至可能预防痴呆症的发生。

sentences.en: The University of Miami’s Galvin advises people to exercise, avoid obesity and control blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 迈阿密大学的加尔文建议人们进行锻炼、避免肥胖并控制血压。

sentences.en: He noted that, "What's good for your heart is good for your brain.”
sentences.zh: 他指出，"对心脏有益的东西对大脑也有益。"

sentences.en: Stay socially and cognitively active, too, Galvin said.
sentences.zh: 同时，也要保持社交和认知活跃，加尔文说。

sentences.en: He urges people to try hearing aids if age brings hearing loss, which can create social isolation.
sentences.zh: 他敦促人们，如果年龄带来听力损失，不妨尝试佩戴助听器，因为这可能造成社交孤立。

sentences.en: He added, "There are things that we have control over, and those things I think would be really, really important to build a better brain as we age."
sentences.zh: 他补充道：'有些是我们能够掌控的，我认为这些对于随着年龄增长打造更健脑的大脑真的、非常重要。'

sentences.en: I’m Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

of, relating to, or involving conscious mental activities (such as thinking, understanding, learning, and remembering)
of or relating to the veins, arteries, etc., that carry fluids (such as blood) through the body
medical. a serious illness caused when a blood vessel in your brain suddenly breaks or is blocked
